Overview

Thornhill sits just north of Steeles Avenue, the boundary between Toronto and York Region. It isn't a municipality on its own: the part west of Yonge is in Vaughan and the part east is in Markham, which affects property tax rates and city services.

It's popular with families who want established neighbourhoods and quick access to Toronto without the city's municipal land transfer tax.

Lifestyle

Mature trees, ravines and parks, with shopping at Promenade and along Yonge. Community centres and places of worship serve a diverse population.

Housing

The historic village area near Yonge and Centre has some of the oldest homes in the region. Much of the rest is detached and semi-detached homes from the 1970s to the 1990s, with newer condos and townhouses along Yonge, Bathurst and Centre Street.

Getting around

  • York Region Transit and Viva rapid transit on Yonge and Highway 7
  • Finch station on Line 1 is a short trip south
  • The Yonge North Subway Extension is planned for this area; check Metrolinx for current timelines
  • Highways 407, 404 and 400 nearby

Amenities & schools

  • Thornhill Village heritage area
  • Promenade Shopping Centre
  • Pomona Mills Park and the Don River trails
  • Thornhill Community Centre

Schools are run by the York Region District School Board and York Catholic District School Board. Boundaries vary street by street; confirm with the board.

Buyers & sellers

If you're buying

  • Check whether the address is in Vaughan or Markham; tax rates and services differ
  • Subway construction may affect some streets near Yonge for a while
  • Older homes may need updates; budget for what an inspection finds
How buying works →

If you're selling

  • Buyers moving north from Toronto are a key audience; highlight the commute and the tax savings
  • Updated kitchens and baths stand out in neighbourhoods of similar-age homes
  • Homes in the heritage area may have rules that need to be disclosed
How selling works →

Investors

Considerations specific to income properties in Thornhill. They're questions to investigate, not predictions.

  • Property tax rates and municipal rules differ between the Vaughan and Markham sides; use the actual municipality in your numbers
  • Secondary-suite rules are set by each city, so confirm what's permitted at the specific address
  • Planned transit can affect future demand, but timing isn't guaranteed; don't build your returns on it
How investment property analysis works →
